newsitem.title: BULGARIA: General Chemical says Bulgaria buy not final.
newsitem.headline: General Chemical says Bulgaria buy not final.

text.p: U.S. firm General Chemical Group said it had not finalised the purchase of a 60 percent stake in Bulgaria's Sodi Devnya soda ash plant, whose sale was announced by a Bulgarian minister last week.
"GCG is continuing to negotiate with the government of Bulgaria for the possible purchase of 60 percent of its Sodi Devnya chemical complex," said a statement sent to Reuters in Sofia.
"GCG has not disclosed any details of its proposal, which is subject to further negotiations and due diligence, nor is the company prepared to confirm published reports of the proposed transaction."

Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Economic Development Roumen Gechev said last week Bulgaria had agreed the sale of a 60 percent stake in Sodi Devnya to General Chemical Group for $160 million and the company had pledged investments of $118 million over the next five years.
The sale would provide a welcome inflow of cash to state coffers, and Gechev's announcement boosted Bulgarian Brady bonds.
Six foreign companies submitted bids to the Privatisation Agency for the sale.

Sodi Devnya exports 10 to 12 percent of the calcinated soda traded in the world. Quarries next to the plant will remain in state hands and the company will have to agree terms with the government for raw material supplies.
Sodi Devnya, which can process 1.2 million tonnes of calcinated soda annually, currently operates at 80 percent of capacity and its net profit for last year was $3.5 million.
Its export markets include the Far East, the Middle East, Latin America and western Europe.
